full_judgment:
10. Mr Halim, in course of his submissions refers to us series of judgments passed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division as well as this Division. He submits that there are series of judgments passed by this Division which confirms that even when workers working for "no work no pay" basis renders service for certain time with an assurance that they would be regularized, they ought to be regularized. The same principles, according to Mr Halim apply in the instant cases. The petitioners have gathered experiences have worked for significant period. There can be no justification for the issuance of the impugned orders. Mr Halim, relying on series of judgments passed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division, also draws our attention to the importance of following the procedural fairness and submits that if executive decisions taken do not conform to the procedural and/or substantive fairness, such decision must be struck down. According to Mr Halim, the impugned orders did not conform to the standard of fairness and, as such, the said orders are illegal. On these counts, he submits that the Rules should be made absolute with appropriate direction upon the respondents. 

 11. The Rules are opposed by the respondents. Affidavits-in-Opposition were filed. It is stated that the appointments were purely temporary, for a limited period of five years and therefore, the petitioners did not have any legitimate expectation to serve the respondents till regular retirement age. The assurance relied upon, being উক্ত ৫ (পোঁচ) বৎসর চাকুরীর মেয়াদ সন্তোষজনক প্রতীয়মান হলে ব্যবস্থাপনা কর্তৃপক্ষ স্বাভাবিক অবসর বয়সসীমা পর্যস্ত আপনার চাকুরীর মেয়াদ বর্ধিত করণের বিষয় বিবেচনা করবেন । is not unconditional; it is for the respondents to decide whether চাকুরীর মেয়াদ would be extended. It was further stated that the instant writ petitions are not maintainable and that the requirement of show cause notice, in the instant cases, is misconceived. It was pointed out that the impugned orders were issued further to a policy decision of the respondents and therefore, this Division should not interfere. 

 15. According to Mr Hasan, the cases referred to by the learned Counsel for the petitioners, in relation to regularization of employees, is not applicable in the instant case because (a) in those cases, there had been concrete representations, either express or by conduct that the employment would be made permanent (b) the employees were made to work for a very long period on the basis of such representations. In the instant case, the letter of appointment and the nature of the organization negatives such representation(s) because the appointment was "periodical" for five years only with an assurance that the case(s) of extension may be considered. In the instant case, extension was not considered because the respondents took a policy decision not to renew terms of employment of all employees employed for a period of five years. 

 16. With regard to the submissions on the need for show cause notice, Mr Hasan points out that in the instant case, such show cause notice is not necessary. According to Mr Hasan, the impugned orders are akin to "termination sirnpliciter" which does not require show cause notice. Further, show cause notice would have been necessary had they been subject to any aspersions, which is not the case here. Mr Hasan points out that the petitioners were all aware of the reason for the issuance of the impugned order which is evident from the fact that in some writ petitions, the order dated 20-3-2017 was annexed; since the legality of the order dated 20-3-2012 was not challenged, the petitioners cannot challenge the legality of the orders impugned. On these counts, Mr Hasan submits that the Rules issued should be discharged. 

 23. In those cases, employees who worked on "no work no pay basis" were given the assurance of subsequent regularization and were made to work for a significant time, all in excess of 5 years. Because of such assurance, they rendered service and gained experience. They ceased to be eligible for appointment in Government posts. Here, the situation is different. The petitioners knew that the extension was not automatic; the petitioners joined the respondents after they retired from the armed forced. The job with the respondents is not the first job. The petitioners were chosen, it seems, after their retirement, so that for certain time, they can work with familiar work environment. In our view, the job offered was a chance/opportunity given to the petitioners, who are otherwise very qualified. We take the view that such opportunity does not necessarily permit the petitioners to rely on the doctrine and insist on renewal of service till regular retirement age. The very nature of the respondent organization coupled with the aforesaid issues we have pointed out, does not give us an impression that it would be unconscionable if the service of the petitioners are not extended till regular retirement age. 

 26. We have, time and time, expressed our view that this Division should be slow to interfere in policy decisions. It is not that we cannot, but we should not unless we see that the policy decision is based on or results in illegality or the policy decision or implementation thereof is manifestly absurd or the policy decision or implementation thereof results in violation of the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution. These exceptional circumstances are not present in the instant case. We therefore, find no reason for interference. Also, the petitioners were aware of this order or even if not, came to be aware since it was annexed in the writ petition. This order was not challenged. The orders issued pursuant to the said order were challenged. That being the position, we are inclined to conclude that the petitioners did not find anything wrong in the order of 20-3-2017 and challenged the orders of removal, just to take a chance to remain in the organization. 

 27. Now, let us address the issue of violation of natural justice, as submitted by Mr Halim. Mr Halim, relying on series of judgments passed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division and this Division pointed out that the impugned orders were not preceded by show cause notice. He also pointed out that even if statutory provision is silent, issuance of show cause notice is mandatory. We are in full agreement with the learned Counsel. Infact, we have passed series of judgments relying on this settled principle. However, there are exceptions to the general principle, affirmed by the apex courts. The issue is whether the case in hand falls within the exception. 

 28. Show cause notice is considered to be minimum obligatory condition. Show cause notice must contain the allegations in clear terms and provide opportunity of being heard. Sometimes, even second show cause notice is mandated and/or desirable. This is to ensure fairness in the administrative decision(s). In the instant case, the impugned orders were issued without casting aspersions on the petitioners. What purpose would a show cause notice, in the instant case, have served? We are not entirely clear. The respondents could have issued a notice to the petitioners stating that a policy decision was taken to remove all employees who joined the service for tenure of five years and sought for an explanation from them as to why they should refrain from taking such policy decision. Such notice was not practical. In our view when policy decision is taken, there is no need for it to be preceded by a show cause notice unless a legislation so requires, in express term. 

 31. Before we part with the judgment, we would wish to summarize our views and findings: (a) We have not been able to come to any conclusion that the respondents have given any assurance expressly and/or impliedly, that the service of the petitioners would be renewed automatically, if they performed satisfactorily; (b) In the instant case, the impugned orders which state that the petitioners performed the service to the full satisfaction of the respondents, in our view, have been issued so that the petitioners can refer this in respect of future job applications; (c) The decisions of the Hon'ble Appellate Division and also this Division, cited by the learned Counsel for the petitioners, on regularization are not relevant in the present case; (d) The impugned orders were issued further to a policy decision not to extend the terms of service of those who were appointed for a period of five years. The said policy decision, based on which the impugned orders were issued, was not challenged. We are therefore, not inclined to interfere with the impugned orders; (e) We are not convinced from the terms of the appointment letter and the fact that the salaries of the petitioners were increased that the petitioners had a legitimate expectation that their services would be renewed. In our view, the plea that there was legitimate expectation that the tenure of service would be extended till regular retirement age is misconceived; (f) In the given facts and circumstances, there was no need to issue any show cause notices to the petitioners; (g) We are convinced that the conduct of the respondents is not discriminatory and the respondents did not adopt "pick and chose" policy in issuing the impugned orders.
